newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: LatAm stocks seen thin ahead of U.S. Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen thin ahead of U.S. Fed meeting.

text.p: Latin American stocks were seen holding their breath ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) meetings on Tuesday and Wednesday which set U.S. interest rates, traders said.

Mexico and Argentina were seen strongly tied to U.S. market movements. Trade volume in Brazil and Venezuela was seen falling ahead of long carnival weekends, while Chilean shares were seen consolidating after a short rally in electricity stocks took the 40-share index up 2.02 percent last week to 110.54 points.
"We see the market somewhat unsettled but without any major swings," said Santiago based Sud Americano broker Lance Eckel.

Due fourth quarter Chilean company results should be better than widely expected, Eckel added. But balanced against that, hopes of an early easing in interest rates are fast fading until later this year when authorities could be certain Chile's robust economic growth has slowed.
In Brazil, an otherwise firm market was seen loosing strength on increased speculation ahead of mid-February options and futures settlements on February 17.
"The market still has room to rise but the risk of buying short before the settlement is high," said one senior trader.
Last week the leading Bovespa index .BVSP rose 2.6 percent to 76,947 points, taking the year's rise to date to 13.1 percent.

In Argentina, the blue-chip MerVal index is seen likely receiving a push from higher than expected tax collection data for January, with $4.1 billion the current market consensus. "Our estimates of $4.32 billion support the government's bullish ($4.4 billion) forecasts," said New York based IDEA in a market commentary.
The index rallied 5.5 percent between last Tuesday and Friday to close at 692.51 points, erasing its previous four day slide on the back of a Wall Street rebound.

In Venezuela, January's generally sluggish trade was seen continuing as foreign investors sit out Caracas equities until the dust settles over on-going labor disputes. Analysts fear 100 percent plus wage claims will burst the budget and send inflation soaring beyond the government's 25 percent 1997 target.
Last week the 19-share index found some bounce on local trade to end up 2.6 percent at 6253.12 points.

In Mexico, thin trade was seen keeping the leading IPC index tightly bound between 3,630 and 3,700 points, with the market wary of inflation data due to be released February 9 as well as the outcome of the FOMC meeting in the United States.
